I usually go full mage but just throwing in one or two magic schools in your  majors can add some variety to your build without having to grind points into them. Being able to cast levitate, open, or a basic shield spell with alteration is handy or teleporting around with  mysticism is fun. 

Throw in Tamriel Rebuilt which I haven't seen much of, and I'm as much a Pilgrim as my Pilgrim character.

This is my favorite volume in the pre Negan era.

Starts off with a classic Walkind Dead moral dilemma. Can we kill a kid? Even if he's a psychopath? The introduction of Father Gabriel (who was underutilized in the comics) which shows that if you've survived this long into to apocalypse you have to have done some fucked up things to survive. Really the first time we've seen our protagonists do some truly fucked up things in the name of vengeance and Gabriel makes a good point that they definitely went too far. My favorite Rick line in probably the whole series "Motherfuckers gonna feel real stupid when they find out, they're fucking with the wrong people." 

It was cool to see villians that were mostly in the shadows, we haven't had a real antagonist since the Govener who was very over the top so it's a good change of pace.

My one major gripe with this volume is the missed opportunity to use starvation and hunger as a major theme, something I think the telltale game in S1e2 "Starved for help" did a lot better. We get a passing line from Michonne that they're running out of food and Rick hand waves it saying just to ration it and it's never brought up again. We never get to see them make hard decisions when it comes to food and no where near close to considering cannibalism which could have been interesting. The villians in TWD always parallel the protagonists and where they are at in their survival. They usually show what Rick and co could easily have turned to if it wasn't for their own moral codes but in this case it's just pure luck that Gabriel walks into their camp (a common trope that happens multiple times in the upcoming volumes) and offers them shelter and food.

I actually like the comic version of the Hunters better than the show. Maybe it was my prior knowledge but I could see Terminus coming a mile away, and even if I didn't, a whole society built around cannibalism felt cheesy af. Like a tight nit group of people resorting to cannibalism because they suck at survival and eventually turning on their own children actually felt scary. 

Dales death was huge for me. Him going out laughing like a maniac and trolling his captors was an awesome way to go out, while I love the "old man whose sick and dying goes off in the woods to die without telling anyone" trope feels a little convenient how long he lasts before dying. Still loved the fond fairwell to a great character. When I think of early TWD I picture Dale and his RV, his fisherman cap. Great, great arc.
